D.t: Jeff Merkley leads by 29.3 in the forecast and wins 100% of simulations. The cushion is about 602,979 votes; a one point swing is about 10,276 voters changing sides.
In 8 of 10 simulations the result lands between D +20.8 and D +37.8. Only an unusual polling error changes the winner.

The biggest vote banks for Democrats: Multnomah, a projected net 303,455 votes; Washington, a projected net 137,658 votes; Lane, a projected net 75,732 votes. Every point of extra turnout here is worth more than persuasion anywhere else.
The large counties within 12 points: Marion, D +11.8, 6.9% of the vote; Jackson, D +11.0, 5.4% of the vote; Yamhill, D +6.7, 2.5% of the vote; Polk, D +10.6, 2.1% of the vote.

D.h: Where you run behind the 2024 map
D.t: Against the 2024 presidential vote, Jeff Merkley runs furthest behind in Douglas, Klamath, Linn. That is where the forecast sees voters who backed your side two years ago and have not come back yet.

Groups big enough to move the race: Voters without a degree, 59% of voters, 59 to 37, where a 5 point gain is worth 2.94 points; Men, 44% of voters, 57 to 39, where a 5 point gain is worth 2.23 points; Voters who can afford daily costs, 38% of voters, 58 to 38, where a 5 point gain is worth 1.91 points.
The forecast's worst groups for Jeff Merkley: Immigration voters 30 to 66, Small counties 46 to 49, Midsize counties 50 to 46. Cutting the loss here is often cheaper than winning new groups.
$6.8M cash against $50K. Spend it early on persuasion television in the battleground counties and keep a reserve for the last week.
